goal: Crafting: find and use every recipe on the crafting screen (C); are tools worth making?

findings.title: Planks and Bricks (2 of 5 recipes) out of reach in ~20 min: Village era needs 10 members; strangers must be Loyal
findings.detail: The crafting screen lists 5 recipes. Axe, Pickaxe and Cooked Meat all work out in the world. Planks x2 and Bricks x2 stay 'Locked: The Workshop is unlocked in the Village era.' I founded a nation and a settlement, built a stall, a house and a farm (Buildings 2/2), and the settlement became a 'Village'. Objective 7 then sat at Members 9/10 for over 6000 ticks. Inviting a nearby stranger with R gave 'Abigail Thomas (Stranger): "I'm loyal to Eastfield." (needs Loyal)'. So the two trade-good recipes, which are the main reason to collect a surplus of wood and stone, stay out of reach for a long time, and nothing on the crafting screen shows how far off they are.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/bn-wt-pt064c --seed 107; gather 50 wood; N; F (outside claimed land); E; B; K K (house); collect stockpile; K K (farm); C -> Planks/Bricks still locked; R on stranger -> needs Loyal

findings.title: Cooked Meat is eaten automatically to top up a few energy points, with no message, while apples are in the bag
findings.detail: Between tick ~6000 and ~6240, energy went from 90 to 99 and cooked_meat went from 1 to 0, while I held 13 apples. No status line said I ate anything, and the second cooked meat I made also disappeared later. Neither the Controls screen nor the Inventory has an Eat action, so the 45-energy food is used up on a 9-point top-up. On top of that, the market buys cooked meat for about 85-93, which is less than the ingredients sell for separately (chicken meat ~47-49 plus wood ~55-57). Right now cooking makes the meat worth less and gives the player no say in when it is eaten. I expected the game to eat apples first, or to let me choose when to eat.
findings.repro: craft Cooked Meat (C, row 3) with energy ~90 and apples in inventory; wait ~5 game seconds; pt state -> cooked_meat gone, energy 99, no status

findings.title: Crafting the axe moves the first objective backwards (Wood 6/10 -> 2/10)
findings.detail: Objective 1 'Gather wood' counts the wood you are carrying, not the wood you have gathered. Crafting an axe (4 wood) right after the first tree dropped the progress from 6/10 to 2/10, so the tutorial penalises the very tool it should encourage.
findings.repro: chop one tree (E); C; click Axe Craft >; close; objective shows Wood 2/10

findings.title: 'The settlement is now a Village!' but crafting says the Workshop needs the Village era (era still Camp)
findings.detail: Right after the farm made my settlement a Village, the crafting header read 'In the Village of Smallton, which has no Workshop: the Workshop is unlocked in the Village era.' The era widget still showed 'Era: Camp (1/4)'. The settlement tier and the nation era are both called 'Village', so the message reads as a contradiction, and a player expects planks and bricks to unlock at this point.
findings.repro: as in the first finding; after 'Farm built. The settlement is now a Village!' press C

findings.title: Objective 7 progress text is cut off ('mbers 8/10'), and it shows Village 0/1 while the era widget shows 0/4
findings.detail: The 'Reach the Village era' progress bar is clipped on the left and shows 'mbers 8/10 . Buildings 0/2'. The body text says 'Village 0/1', while the era widget just above says 'Village: 0/4'.
findings.repro: complete objective 6 (build a stall) and look at the objective panel

findings.title: First tree's status line says '2 apples' but the floating text and inventory show 1
findings.detail: The status said 'Gathered 6 wood and 2 apples from tree.' The floating text said '+1 apple' and the inventory showed Apples: 1. Energy jumped from 84 to 99, so one apple was probably eaten automatically without any message.

findings.title: Very low frame and tick rate (fps 0-5, tps 0.8-22) makes menus slow to respond
findings.detail: Measured with several sessions sharing the machine. Era-widget clicks never opened a visible panel, a stockpile click sometimes did nothing on the first try, and game time ran at about 1/3 speed or slower.

verdict: Tools are clearly worth making. The axe adds +3 wood to a base of about 4-6 per tree (about 65% more) and pays back its 4 wood within 2 trees, and the pickaxe adds +2 to a base of 5 stone. The crafting screen explains costs, readiness, uses left and locks very well. But only 3 of 5 recipes can be used early: Planks and Bricks sit behind a Village era that needs 10 loyal members. Cooked Meat is a trap: it is auto-eaten for small top-ups, there is no Eat control, and it sells for less than its ingredients.
